notes: Relation types and modifiers, loaded by medkg.config. Override with
MEDKG_ONTOLOGY=/path/to/ontology.json or run.py --ontology.
Every relation's head/tail refers to a SPAN LABEL, and a span label only
exists if some configured NER model emits it. `ner_models` below is the
map from each model's raw labels onto this ontology's vocabulary; a
relation whose head or tail is not reachable from ANY configured model can
never fire, however well phrased its gloss. `medkg.ontology.validate`
reports exactly that, and it is the first thing to check when extraction
yield is low.
`uri` uses CURIEs expanded by medkg.ontology: ont: sct: rxn:.
`source` names the external vocabulary the type corresponds to. Where a
numeric identifier is not stated it has deliberately NOT been guessed --
build_ontology.py --from-srdef fills real UMLS Semantic Network
identifiers in from your own NET/SRDEF and NET/SRSTRE2 files.
`subPropertyOf` names a more general relation type. Stage 2 asserts only
the most specific type that fits and drops the parent (guards.
prune_subsumed_relations); Stage 7 emits the rdfs:subPropertyOf axiom and
materializes the parent into urn:graph:inferred, so the general fact stays
queryable but is marked derived rather than claimed.
`label_hierarchy` maps a span label to a more general one. A head/tail
constraint is satisfied by the label itself or any ancestor, so a type set
can be written once in general terms instead of enumerating every NER
vocabulary that might reach it.
`aliases` are other names for the SAME relation; `inverseOf` are names for
the relation read from the other end, and Stage 2 accepts them by swapping
head and tail. Extractors reach for an inverse when the menu only offers one
direction -- a run produced produced_by, stored_in, required_for and
affected_by, all of which were discarded as unknown types.
`catalyzes` takes a Protein head, not any Substance: catalysis is done by
enzymes, and the looser set let T3 and iodine through once Drug became a
kind of Substance. A type constraint that contradicts its own gloss is a
bug in the constraint.

head: Disease
treated_with.gloss: HEAD is the disease, TAIL is the drug. 'X treated_with Y' means Y TREATS X.

head: Disease
prevented_by.gloss: HEAD is the disease, TAIL is the drug. 'X prevented_by Y' means Y PREVENTS X.

head: Disease
Finding
Morphology
caused_by.gloss: HEAD is the EFFECT, TAIL is the CAUSE. 'X caused_by Y' means Y CAUSES X. For 'hyperthyroidism leads to osteoporosis', write osteoporosis caused_by hyperthyroidism -- NOT the reverse. This holds for NOMINAL phrasing too: 'Graves' disease is a frequent cause of hyperthyroidism' is hyperthyroidism caused_by Graves' disease, and 'the most common cause is Hashimoto's' puts Hashimoto's in the TAIL. If the cause is an abnormal amount of something ('a deficiency in dietary iodine', 'an excess of thyroid hormones'), the tail needs a `deviation` modifier -- iodine alone as the tail says iodine causes goiter, which is the opposite of the truth.

head: Protein
catalyzes.gloss: HEAD is the ENZYME, TAIL is the reaction's substrate or product -- never an atom or group transferred within it. For 'deiodinases catalyze the conversion of T4 to T3 by removing iodine atoms' the tail is T4 or T3, not iodine.

deviation.source: local; map to a SNOMED qualifier value in production -- no identifier is guessed here (see HANDOFF 9.7)
deviation.gloss: Direction of abnormality for a substance, hormone or process: deficiency, excess or resistance. THE MOST IMPORTANT MODIFIER IN THIS FILE -- it is the difference between 'iodine causes goiter' and 'iodine deficiency causes goiter'. Extract it whenever the text says deficiency, insufficient, lack of, excess, excessive, elevated, too much/little, over- or underproduction.
